races.name: Kilmore Quay (C & G) Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Plastic Paddy
runners_data.note: Hold-up type, 8yo with two hurdle pulls (PP) on recent flat form, fades in finish tag is a concern over 2m½f on Good; 21 days fresh but limited jumping form suggests mere participation.|

runners_data.name: Among The Pines
runners_data.note: Brian Hayes partner for Kieran Callaghan; finished 11th on debut over hurdles at this trip on Good — its natural rear-of-field style means it will need something to go wrong up front in a race with no real pressure on the leader.|

runners_data.name: Chasing Blues
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead and Darragh O'Keeffe combine with a horse whose best hurdle run was a 4th on Good over 2m4f — its hold-up instincts are genuine but it has been pushed toward midfield on the map simply because the field is top-heavy with closers; best chance of all the rear-runners if daylight appears in the straight.|

runners_data.name: Colwyn Bay
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for P J Rothwell who fades in the finish and has pulled up or run poorly on Good ground recently; Mr R Sugrue (7lb claimer) reduces the weight but the form (30-F0) is discouraging and its true waiting style makes this steady-pace race awkward.|

runners_data.name: Drumconnor Hill
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 5yo for Cian Collins with an unknown tactical profile (style=U); placed 4th and 8th in only two hurdle starts both on Good, and Ben Harvey takes the ride — the unexposed angle is the main interest here.|

runners_data.name: Highland Realm
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner, trained by W P Mullins, with a 2nd and a 5th from two hurdling starts both on Good; Sean O'Keeffe rides and the horse gets an uncontested lead in a field that cannot mount genuine early pressure — this is the race shape's pivotal horse.|

runners_data.name: Owl's Delight
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old returning after 269 days off for R Donohoe; form reads 9F8P with a pull-up, and its hold-up style in a steady-paced race makes it very hard to fancy on comeback.|

runners_data.name: Penny Express
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends Jack Kennedy — always a significant combination — on a mare that has placed three times over hurdles including recent 4th and 5th on Good; prominent style suits tracking Highland Realm directly and the booking strengthens the case.|

runners_data.name: Betterluckthistime
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with just two career hurdle starts (9th and 12th) for P J Rothwell; its true closer profile is squeezed toward midfield on the pace map, and the very thin form base makes improvement hard to quantify — Shane O'Callaghan (3lb claim) is the only positive.|

runners_data.name: Blue Nude
runners_data.note: Another Rothwell 4yo with only two outings (8th and 16th on Good); its genuine waiting style gets little help from a race run at a controlled tempo, and the form to date offers minimal encouragement.|

runners_data.name: Finjimk
runners_data.note: Liam McKenna (3lb claim) rides this Peter John Flood-trained 4yo who ran 8th and 7th in two Good-ground hurdles; its natural hold-up style is compressed toward midfield by the field's make-up, and it is one of the more forward-travelling of the true closers if it can get into a rhythm early.|

runners_data.name: Game Point
runners_data.note: R P Cody's 4yo has the most consistent recent form in the race (3-2-3 last three) over 16-18f on Good; Donagh Meyler rides and the horse's prominent-ish style suits sitting just behind Highland Realm — a reliable each-way profile in this shape.|

runners_data.name: Pinkarizon
runners_data.note: Padraig Butler's 4yo wears headgear (hood/tongue-tie combination) and has two hurdle pulls on form; its natural rear-of-field style and modest back form (5th and 13th on flat) leave Phillip Enright with plenty to do.|

runners_data.name: Plus Or Minus
runners_data.note: P A Fahy's 4yo is stepping up from 12-13f to 2m½f; the form on soft/good-to-soft has been moderate (7-8-9-11) and the fade-in-finish tag is a concern on this step up in trip — tongue-tie applied.|

runners_data.name: Megaball
runners_data.note: Francis Casey's 4yo has a single hurdle run (pulled up on Good over 18f); Reserve jockey listed, which adds uncertainty, and the completely unknown profile over this trip makes assessment speculative.|

runners_data.name: Texas Red
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's 6yo with five hurdle runs showing 4-5-5-6-8 form, most on Good ground; an unknown tactical profile (style=U) and reserve jockey assigned means this is a wildcard with no strong angle.|

races.paceDynamic: Highland Realm is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner maiden hurdle and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from flag to finish over the 2m½f Wexford trip on Good ground. Penny Express and Game Point are the most credible prominent types likely to track Highland Realm through the early stages, creating a small lead group but no meaningful pressure on the pace-setter. The field behind is stacked with hold-up horses — Among The Pines, Chasing Blues, Colwyn Bay, Finjimk, Betterluckthistime, Blue Nude, and Pinkarizon all have natural hold-up profiles but have been pushed forward on the map because there is simply no room for them all at the rear; of these, Chasing Blues and Finjimk are most likely to actually secure a position closer to the pace. This race shape strongly favours a prominent racer who can travel comfortably behind Highland Realm and produce a measured late challenge, or the front-runner itself if the gallop stays genuinely unhurried — hold-up horses racing against their natural style face a stern test of getting competitive in a steadily-run affair.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Highland Realm Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Highland Realm sets a comfortable, uncontested pace and the prominent trackers never build enough momentum to reel it in on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Highland Realm, trained by W P Mullins and ridden by Sean O'Keeffe, has the course and distance form, sets its own fractions with no rival willing to burn it up, and a Good surface suits — a lone leader in a 16-runner field over 2m½f with a weak pace map behind it is a formidable combination.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough that Highland Realm ties up in the final half-mile and a close-up tracker picks it off at the last.
scenarios.body: Penny Express (Jack Kennedy, Gordon Elliott) and Game Point (Donagh Meyler) are the natural beneficiaries, sitting a length or two off the leader and needing only a slight tempo increase to collar a tiring front-runner; Game Point's consistent 2-3-3 recent form at this trip on Good is directly relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Threads Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race, the field strings out, and a hold-up horse that genuinely gets its position produces a finishing burst in the final flight.
scenarios.body: Chasing Blues (De Bromhead/Darragh O'Keeffe) is the most credible genuine hold-up type here with a recent 4th on Good and a strong handler combination that suggests a fit, well-prepared horse; if it finds clear daylight from the back of the field in the straight it is the most dangerous late mover, though the steady pace makes this route harder than it looks.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Mover Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If an unexposed or lightly-raced runner — particularly one making only its second or third start — improves sharply past its current form figures.
scenarios.body: Drumconnor Hill (5yo, 2 hurdle runs, modest form but lightly raced) and Betterluckthistime (4yo, only 2 career starts) represent the unknown quantities in this field; either could improve enough to be competitive but needs the race to be run in a way that exposes the veterans' limitations.

watchPoints.text: Highland Realm's uncontested lead is the defining factor — watch whether Sean O'Keeffe elects to ping off immediately or settles briefly, as any increase in early tempo could compromise its stamina at the 2m½f trip.

Penny Express (Jack Kennedy/Gordon Elliott) arriving fresh off a 13-day turnaround with three career places is the most dangerous prominent tracker — watch its jumping fluency from the fourth flight onwards as a guide to whether it can challenge in the straight.

Game Point's consistent placed form (3-2-3) makes it a quiet danger; watch Donagh Meyler's positioning in the early stages — if it slots in second or third by the top of the back straight it becomes a serious threat to the leader.

Chasing Blues is the most credible of the hold-up horses if the pace quickens unexpectedly — watch whether Darragh O'Keeffe opts to push forward early rather than accept a rear position in a field where the back is very congested.

With five P J Rothwell runners (Colwyn Bay, Betterluckthistime, Blue Nude, Texas Red and Megaball) the stable is essentially fielding a team — watch for any market move on Colwyn Bay or Texas Red in-running as a stableyard signal.

races.name: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On August 29th Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bold Reflection
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old for McConnell with a win over 2m on good ground at the Curragh and solid form at this trip; prominent style suits the likely race shape but the horse's recent finish positions (4th, pulled up) after a long absence warrant respect over fitness.|

runners_data.name: Lilannbee
runners_data.note: Carey-trained hold-up horse with a win at 2m2f on good ground and Listed-placed form, though a 110-day absence and the redistribution to midfield — her natural rearward style squeezed by the volume of hold-up types in this field — mean she will not get her optimum tactical pitch.|

runners_data.name: Are You Around
runners_data.note: Mullins runner ridden by Brian Hayes, placed twice in three hurdle starts including a 2m4f run on good; the 272-day absence is the key risk but class and tactical versatility give this one a leading profile in the dominant race shape.|

runners_data.name: Cailin Hill
runners_data.note: Debutante hurdles runner who finished tenth over 2m on good ground 13 days ago; a finisher who tends to fade late, and the horse's true hold-up style is constrained by the crowded rear division — hard to fancy on current evidence.|

runners_data.name: Jolly D'olivate
runners_data.note: Has won over fences but the hurdles form — a string of pulled-up and fell entries — is uninspiring; a fader who cannot access her natural back-of-field position in this congested field, and the 9-day turnaround adds a further question mark.|

runners_data.name: Louve d'Arc
runners_data.note: William Harvey-trained five-year-old whose three hurdle runs have produced no better than fourth; genuine hold-up style but without the class angles of the market principals and a 128-day layoff to overcome.|

runners_data.name: Lunar Majesty
runners_data.note: Murphy-trained mare with a placed effort at 2m4f on soft; her natural sit-and-wait approach is compressed by the rear-division traffic, though her trip experience gives her a stamina edge if the race develops into a genuine test.|

runners_data.name: Miss Jocund
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's consistent mare (three top-five finishes on good ground including two thirds) with headgear noted; a reliable but not explosive finisher whose consistent jumping and fitness make her a solid each-way profile in the dominant shape.|

runners_data.name: Red Sea Girl
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner for Stokes; has placed three times in four good-ground hurdle starts and leads naturally, but the STYLE_FIT flag reminds that dictating may not suit her as much as tracking — nonetheless she is structurally critical to this pace map.|

runners_data.name: Thesilverbridle
runners_data.note: Second McConnell runner, unexposed after three starts including a fall; lightly raced tag means going preference is unknown, and the 102-day break adds to the uncertainty, but the trainer's second string could outrun a price if jumping is clean.|

runners_data.name: Urra Mass Rock
runners_data.note: Seymour's hold-up fader who finished tenth over 2m6f on good ground 39 days ago; nothing in the form book to suggest a turnaround and the natural hold-up style is further marginalised by the crowded rear.|

runners_data.name: Burning Like Fire
runners_data.note: Hogan's lightly raced four-year-old with a single third on the flat; an entirely unknown quantity over hurdles and carrying the lightest weight, making this a speculative entry whose chance is hard to assess but not impossible to dismiss.|

runners_data.name: Gratitudeforgrace
runners_data.note: Elliott's debutante hurdles runner who finished last of 12 over 2m on good recently; a natural hold-up horse pushed into the midfield cluster by the rear-division congestion, and nothing from that run to inspire confidence here.|

runners_data.name: My Girl Rosie
runners_data.note: Donoghue's four-year-old who has finished 5th, 9th, 8th in three hurdle starts on good going; a hold-up fader with no wins or places and no obvious angle to reverse that pattern over the longer trip.|

runners_data.name: Queenofqueenstreet
runners_data.note: Reserve runner for Sheehy; last of 15 on her only start over hurdles on good ground 377 days ago, with a massive layoff to overcome — needs dramatic improvement to factor.|

runners_data.name: Tubberfinn Lassie
runners_data.note: Reserve runner for Carr; tongue-tied eight-year-old whose last two starts were pulled ups, followed by a 277-day break — the form profile and age make this a very difficult proposition.|

runners_data.name: Runaway Rosie
runners_data.note: Reserve Mullins runner who finished last of 15 over 2m on good ground 318 days ago; the trainer is the only positive but a year off the track and a poor debut mean this is a hard case to make on form alone.|

races.paceDynamic: Red Sea Girl is the one confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner mares' maiden hurdle over 2m4f at Wexford, and with no genuine rival willing to press her for the lead, she is set to bowl along at a comfortable, self-regulated tempo on good ground. The field is unusually loaded with hold-up types — Lilannbee, Jolly D'olivate, Gratitudeforgrace, Cailin Hill, Lunar Majesty and others are all natural rear-division horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the pace map simply because they cannot all occupy the back of the field in practice; in reality, several will be bunched in a chasing pack rather than covering ground from off the pace. With Red Sea Girl able to dictate an uncontested, honest-but-not-brutal gallop, this race shape strongly favours prominent or mid-division horses with the stamina and jumping ability to travel smoothly in behind before launching a sustained challenge from two out — a truly flat-finishing sprint finish is unlikely given the 2m4f trip on good going, so pure hold-up closers who need a truly end-to-end gallop to deliver their best are at a structural disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Late Pressed
scenarios.trigger: If Red Sea Girl dictates an uncontested pace and the chasers track her within striking range before a genuine two-out battle develops.
scenarios.body: Red Sea Girl sets the fractions she wants and arrives at the final two hurdles full of running, with the prominent-travelling types behind her only able to reduce the deficit in the closing stages rather than sweep past cleanly; prominent and mid-division horses with the stamina and jumping fluency to stay close throughout are best positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent contingent travelling just off Red Sea Girl's shoulder — particularly from the Mullins and McConnell yards — produce a smooth move from three out and overhaul the leader on the run to the last.
scenarios.body: Are You Around's class (Mullins, Brian Hayes) and Bold Reflection's experience at this trip allow them to time their runs off the controlled pace and hit the front at the last hurdle; this shape rewards horses with tactical speed and class advantages over raw staying power.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Plays Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens appreciably from four out and a grinding stamina test develops, exposing any horse short of fitness or distance experience.
scenarios.body: Horses proven at 2m4f-plus on good ground with peak fitness hold an edge as the field strings out and the winner comes from a horse that simply stays on strongest; Lunar Majesty's 2m6f experience and Miss Jocund's consistent placing record give them a fitness-backed profile for this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset From The Pack
scenarios.trigger: If a lightly-raced or unknown type — Burning Like Fire, Thesilverbridle — produces a career-best round of jumping to emerge late from the chasing group.
scenarios.body: Lightly raced horses carrying the smallest weights with unexposed profiles can occasionally produce a significant step forward when conditions suit and experience is not the determining factor; this scenario is low probability given the redistribution congestion in mid-pack and the dependence on horses whose form is entirely unknown.

watchPoints.text: Red Sea Girl's jumping is the pivotal watch point — if she gets in a tangle at an early hurdle and loses the lead, there is no natural replacement pace-setter and the race shape collapses entirely.

The sheer volume of hold-up types attempting to share midfield from flagfall creates a significant risk of scrimmaging and interference on the first circuit; horses drawn wide or caught in traffic approaching the first bend — particularly Jolly D'olivate, Gratitudeforgrace and Cailin Hill — are vulnerable to losing ground.

Are You Around is unraced for 272 days and while the Mullins yard is reliable with returning types, any sign of ring-rustiness or a jumping mistake from two out would dramatically change the likely outcome given this horse's place in the market.

Bold Reflection (eight years old, recent pulled-up run) and Lunar Majesty (39 days since last run) both carry fitness questions despite their experience at the trip — watch the early market moves for any sign of market confidence in either, which would upgrade their probability meaningfully.

Reserve runners Queenofqueenstreet, Tubberfinn Lassie and Runaway Rosie would only enter the race if multiple withdrawals occur; if the field slims to below 12, the pace dynamic shifts and Red Sea Girl's front-running advantage becomes even more pronounced.

races.name: Wexford Racecourse Ladies Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: An Peann Dearg
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer who needs cover and a strong pace to deliver her best; recent form shows a string of poor finishes including two pull-ups, and at 9 years old on a 23-day turnaround, her chance looks slim in a steady-pace race where ground from the rear is hard to make.|

runners_data.name: Jonny Carrol
runners_data.note: Unclassified style (U), has placed at 22f on Good going and returns after 57 days; modest form at the top of recent starts but showed a placed effort at 22f in Good conditions which gives a small foothold here.|

runners_data.name: Harpy Eagle
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner; Paul Nolan's stable at 0/5 in the past 14 days is a flag, but she holds the pivotal tactical role — if she stays sound and travels kindly, her position on the front end is an enormous asset even if her style-fit score (0.92) nudges against over-relying on her winning.|

runners_data.name: Midleton Rare
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 24f Good-ground trip in her recent history and is a natural prominent horse; returning after 68 days for Noel Kelly with hurdle headgear in her profile, she has the course-and-distance form that others lack and is well suited to the likely race shape.|

runners_data.name: Costanuci
runners_data.note: Consistent front-rank type without a win in the past 15 Good-ground starts; ran just 13 days ago and is on a very quick turnaround — high likelihood of holding a prominent pitch but questionable whether she has the class or freshness to convert.|

runners_data.name: Sean Mc
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win at 20f on Good going and strong recent placed efforts; trained by Paul Nolan (0/4 in 14 days, a mild flag) but his style and distance profile align closely with what this pace map rewards — a leading contender from the front rank.|

runners_data.name: Empire Walk
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent and at ease on Good ground; has been placed at 22f and 24f, returns after 58 days and brings consistent form figures — sits in the right place on the map to travel smoothly and challenge late if the pace is even.|

runners_data.name: Double Power
runners_data.note: Has finished in the lower half of the field in all five recent Good-ground outings; no win and no place on similar conditions, and a 17-day turnaround for a horse who has not fired suggests limited claims in a competitive 16-runner field.|

runners_data.name: Matter Of Opinion
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 203 days off — the extended layoff is the dominant concern; placed at 24f on Good going in better days, but needs the race to produce a searching test and needs significant race fitness that may not be present after seven months.|

runners_data.name: Je Suis
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 26f on Good ground and showed a close-up third just 11 days ago; drops back to 24f here, which may actually suit better, and is a hold-up type who travels well enough to sit within striking distance — one of the more interesting profiles off the back.|

runners_data.name: Ladiam
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer who has placed six times at this level in Good conditions, including wins; the field congestion means she cannot hold her natural pitch and is mapped to midfield — her 1W6P record on similar going shows consistency but her chance is tempered by racing out of role.|

runners_data.name: Ocean Murphy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse and the youngest in the field at 4; ran nine days ago and has limited Good-ground experience, with most form coming on Soft or Heavy — Good going is an unknown quantity and the youth and recent run count against.|

runners_data.name: Stumblin In
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago — an extremely quick turnaround — and all five recent Good-ground outings have ended in finishes of 6th or worse; her true hold-up style is further compromised by being redistributed to midfield on the map, and the combination of fatigue and positional concession makes her claims very slim.|

runners_data.name: Larkins Lane
runners_data.note: Has won twice on Soft and Good-to-Soft but both Good-ground runs produced 8th and 9th; her natural front-rank style cannot be fully expressed in this deep prominent field and the trainer (Rothwell, 1/21 in 14 days) has a moderate recent record — the redistribution effectively neutralises her best weapon.|

runners_data.name: China Grill
runners_data.note: Carries a finishing fade flag, has finished 10th or worse in all four recent Good-ground starts, and her redistributed position means she is not even running from her most comfortable spot — a combination of poor form, unfavourable going profile and out-of-role mapping leaves her with very little to recommend.|

races.paceDynamic: Harpy Eagle is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner field and, critically, faces no pressure for the lead — she can dictate her own rhythm throughout the 2m4f trip on Good ground at Wexford, setting a sustainable rather than searingly fast pace. With Midleton Rare, Sean Mc, Costanuci, Empire Walk and Double Power all naturally prominent types, there is a significant surplus of horses wanting to race close to the pace; Ladiam and Larkins Lane are genuine front-rank horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there simply is not room for all of them to hold their natural position — Harpy Eagle, Sean Mc and Midleton Rare are best placed to actually secure prominent berths. The likely result is a controlled, single-file procession from the front with a moderate gallop, meaning the race will be run to suit horses who travel close to the pace and have enough left to quicken approaching the final hurdle, rather than deep closers who need an extreme test of stamina. Hold-up horses such as An Peann Dearg, Matter Of Opinion and Coolboy Christy face a straightforward question: can they make up ground on a field that will not have emptied its tanks early? This race shape firmly favours prominent-to-midfield travellers who can produce a well-timed challenge over the final two flights — true hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Harpy Eagle sets an uncontested, even gallop and the race is never truly run at a testing pace.
scenarios.body: Harpy Eagle dictates every yard, conserving enough energy to fight back or a nearby prominent runner picks her off after the last; the steady tempo means horses who travel in the first four or five race without having to chase or burn fuel. Sean Mc and Midleton Rare are ideally placed to pounce, having competed at this trip in Good ground and showing the requisite class to hold a position and quicken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Modest Pace, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the steady gallop strings the field out and a tracking midfield horse produces a sustained run from two out.
scenarios.body: A moderate pace on Good ground at 2m4f leaves enough in the tank for a horse sitting just off the leaders to produce a powerful finishing run from the second-last; Je Suis and Coolboy Christy, both comfortable on Good and placed on their best form at this sort of trip, are the profiles who benefit here. Je Suis in particular has placed twice over 26f on Good going and can quicken off a slow tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Picks Up, Hold-Up Denied
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that true hold-up horses cannot bridge the gap from the rear.
scenarios.body: A genuine gallop, even if set by Harpy Eagle alone, can string the field over Wexford's tight track and leave horses who are forced wide or back with too much ground to make up; An Peann Dearg and Matter Of Opinion need a truly searching test to get competitive, and if the race does not accelerate sufficiently from the rear their finishing efforts will be blunted. In this shape the race still goes to a prominent type, but horses who have been shuffled back through redistribution may frustrate their supporters.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Redistributed Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes crowding early and some of the redistributed prominent types force their way to the front, unsettling the expected order.
scenarios.body: With 16 runners, early congestion could allow Ladiam or Larkins Lane to push forward aggressively from their mapped midfield positions, potentially setting a faster, more contested pace than Harpy Eagle alone would choose; this altered dynamic could open the door for an unexpectedly strong finisher, but because these horses are racing out of role the scenario remains low probability. The style-fit discount on Ladiam and Larkins Lane means this shape is unlikely to resolve cleanly in favour of either.

watchPoints.text: Harpy Eagle holds the race by the throat — watch the early stages to see whether she escapes unchallenged or whether Ladiam and Larkins Lane push forward from their mapped positions to contest the lead and change the tempo entirely.

Stumblin In ran just two days ago; watch for signs of distress or fatigue in the parade ring and early in the race — a horse racing so quickly back on Good ground over 2m4f with 15 rivals is a significant safety concern as well as a race-shape factor.

The 16-runner field at tight Wexford over 2m4f on Good ground creates real crowding risk at the first few flights — watch for early fallers or horses losing position that could disrupt the natural running order, particularly around the redistributed prominent types fighting for space.

Matter Of Opinion returns from 203 days off — watch her in the parade for any signs of ring-rustiness or lack of condition; if she shows well pre-race she may outrun a big price, but she needs the race to develop into a stamina test to be involved.|

Sean Mc's jockey Sarah Kavanagh (claiming 4lb) has not been flagged for recent trainer form concerns beyond the Nolan 0/4 window — watch how confidently she deploys him in the early stages; if she settles him just off Harpy Eagle's shoulder, he is positioned to dictate the finish.|

races.name: Cottage Autism Network Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Charlie's Dilemma
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, John McConnell's 7yo has five recent runs at 22f+ on Good ground without a win but consistently competes at the sharp end; the STYLE_FIT flag notes she races out of a purely prominent role here as actual leader, but her ability to control tempo is the defining tactical fact of this race.

runners_data.name: Jury Foreman
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's 5yo shows a "U" (unseated) in recent form and has not run for 57 days, both significant flags; shaped as unknown style with no clear positional signature across recent Goodground starts, making him a genuine risk factor over three miles.

runners_data.name: Gerrys Wish
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott on this 5yo, who has placed twice at 24f on Good ground and clearly stays the trip; likely to settle just off Charlie's Dilemma and is well-placed to kick when it matters with the best jockey in the field.

runners_data.name: Barryroe Madam
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who has one win from 15 similar-going starts; recent form reads 300-00 which is uninspiring, but she stays three miles and Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim helps offset a 158lb burden — she needs things to go wrong ahead of her.

runners_data.name: John Storey
runners_data.note: A prominent-going 8yo who has not run for 102 days and failed to finish in his last two starts; headgear (tongue-tie/cheekpieces) suggests trainer is trying to find a solution, but the long absence and non-completion record make him hard to trust over this trip.

runners_data.name: Ersudaly
runners_data.note: Colin Bowe's 6yo has run just nine days ago and shows an "F" (fell) in recent form over shorter trips; he is held up by style but has never won and his Going record here shows only three competitive runs from six — the quick reappearance is a query.

runners_data.name: Ellens Pride
runners_data.note: Phillip Enright partners this 6yo, who carries a "fades in finish" flag that is a serious concern over three miles; recent best effort was a win over shorter, and the step up to 3m on Good ground looks like a question mark against his stamina.

runners_data.name: Ballinaboola Hanna
runners_data.note: A 5yo hold-up filly who fell last time out (F in recent form) and has been off 100 days; only one of six similar-going starts has been competitive, and Richard Deegan takes the ride on a horse whose profile screams inexperience at this level.

runners_data.name: True Harmony
runners_data.note: Seamus Neville's 6yo carries a fade flag and is a natural hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map slot because the rear positions are oversubscribed; his best recent run was a 2nd over 24f on Good ground, which shows the ability is there if he can get a clear run, though his STYLE_FIT discount applies.

runners_data.name: Fervida
runners_data.note: Ross Berry (7) partners this 6yo who shows P89P-9 in recent form and fades late — a deeply problematic combination for a 3m handicap hurdle; no trainer data attached and the form suggests she will likely be a non-factor from the home turn.

runners_data.name: Katie's Casper
runners_data.note: Patrick M O'Brien (5) rides for Dermot McLoughlin; this 7yo has placed twice over 24f on Good ground and stays the trip, but as a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield due to field congestion, she will need a muddling race to find the gaps her style demands.

runners_data.name: Lady Victrix
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's 6yo has been off 178 days — the longest layoff in the field — and carries a fade flag; as a hold-up type unable to get her natural position in this large field, the combination of absence, style compromise, and stamina concern makes her very difficult to back.

runners_data.name: Hob's Angel
runners_data.note: Donagh Meyler partners James Barcoe's 10yo, who won at 20f on Good ground recently and has placed three times from 15 similar-going starts; at OR 77 he is well-handicapped relative to recent form, and his prominent style gives him the tactical position to be competitive if he reproduces that recent win.

runners_data.name: Set The Tone
runners_data.note: Conor Stone-Walsh rides this 5yo for David O'Brien; a genuine hold-up type shuffled into midfield on the map, his best recent run was a 2nd over 22f on Good ground which shows ability, but he will need the race to develop in a way that gives true closers a run — the STYLE_FIT discount applies.

runners_data.name: Strong Contender
runners_data.note: Norman Lee's 5yo ran just two days ago — the sharpest turnaround in the field — and carries both a fade flag and a STYLE_FIT discount as a genuine hold-up horse mapped out of position; form of F0-078 shows little, and Reserve 1 jockey booking adds further uncertainty.

races.paceDynamic: Charlie's Dilemma is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner 3m handicap hurdle, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, she can dictate an unhurried, controlled tempo on Good ground at Wexford. Gerrys Wish, John Storey, and Hob's Angel are the prominent types most likely to track close, while the hold-up contingent is large and heavily redistributed — True Harmony, Katie's Casper, Lady Victrix, Set The Tone, and Strong Contender are all genuine hold-up horses who will be unable to settle as far back as their natural style demands in a field this size at this trip. With a single pace-setter setting a sustainable gallop over three miles, the race shape strongly favours horses who can travel close to the action from the outset and kick at the second-last, rather than those forced to make ground from further back than ideal. The field holds materially more hold-up horses than the rear positions can accommodate, and Gerrys Wish, Hob's Angel, and John Storey are best placed to physically secure the prominent berths that matter.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Charlie's Dilemma sets a steady, uncontested pace and the prominent trackers conserve energy to strike from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Charlie's Dilemma rolls along at a sustainable clip, and the horses tracking two to four lengths off the pace have first run on the field turning for home; with no pace injection mid-race, prominent types who travel sweetly get first crack at the prize.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Charlie's Dilemma extends her advantage at the top of the straight and the big field leaves pursuers with traffic problems.
scenarios.body: A messy, bunched mid-race with 15 runners means those waiting for gaps in the straight are left flat-footed, and Charlie's Dilemma — already clear and jumping well — finds enough in the tank to last home over three miles on Good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a clear run for a true closer to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Despite the redistribution issue, a horse like Katie's Casper or Set The Tone — who has form figures of 2 in similar conditions — could find daylight if the field fans wide on the home turn; this is a lower-probability shape because several of these runners are not truly able to settle as deep as their style demands.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Scramble Late
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the pace and the race degenerates into a messy staying test in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: With Jury Foreman and Ersudaly showing non-completions in their recent form, a disrupted race where early leaders tire and rivals are impeded could see a tenacious stayer grind past rivals close home; Barryroe Madam's ability to stay this trip and Ballinaboola Hanna's 5-year-old freshness could become relevant.

watchPoints.text: Charlie's Dilemma sets every pace parameter in this race — if she jumps cleanly and bowls along at a sustainable clip, horses unable to get close to her early (particularly the redistributed hold-up types) may simply never land a blow.

Strong Contender ran only two days ago and is partnered by Reserve 1 jockey; a horse this fresh in the cycling sense, with a hold-up style it cannot execute, is a non-completion risk worth monitoring for its effect on rivals mid-race.

Jury Foreman showed an unseated rider recently and returns after 57 days for Paul Nolan — with 15 runners in a 3m hurdle, any jumping incident from this type of risk horse in the pack could compromise prominent racers directly behind.

Hob's Angel won over 20f on Good ground recently and his prominent style puts him in the right place at the right time in this race shape — watch whether Donagh Meyler positions him close enough to Charlie's Dilemma to have first run turning in.

Gerrys Wish has placed twice at 24f on Good ground and Jack Kennedy's positional judgment will be key — watch where Kennedy slots him in the early stages, as a position in the first three or four will define whether this horse can deliver its form.

races.name: Cottage Autism Network Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Desert Cave
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for G Ahern, returning 13 days after a run over a similar 3m trip on Good — his sim-going record of 1W 2P from 11 starts on this surface is modest but consistent, and at 8 years old his jumping experience is his main asset; trip suits but winning form is elusive.

runners_data.name: Moonlight Paradise
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for Paul Nolan who has shown enough to place at this level on Good ground but has yet to win over hurdles; a natural hold-up type who goes well fresh (21 days off), though his sole notable placing on similar going came over a shorter trip and the 3m test is a question mark.

runners_data.name: Georgia Celena
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in the race and likely to stride clear from flagfall, though her STYLE_FIT flag is a reminder that she has form issues when conditions force her to race prominently rather than dominate; John McConnell's charge has winning form over similar trips on Good and her jumping will be key to how long she can sustain the lead.

runners_data.name: Fire Coral
runners_data.note: Stuart Curling's seven-year-old has a sharp record on Good ground — 15 from 15 sim-going runs show 2W 4P — and he has won twice at 24f, making the 3m trip credible; races prominently by nature and has the consistent form to be dangerous in a race dominated by a controlled gallop.

runners_data.name: Nashville Notions
runners_data.note: Off 48 days, this hold-up performer for Paul Stephen Kiely has a modest record at the back of fields and his recent form string of P, U, 5, 8, 0 is concerning; sim-going placed form exists but the long break and habit of finishing midfield suggest confidence is needed.

runners_data.name: Keep The Head
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is a significant concern over 3m on Good ground at this stage of the season; John Joseph Hanlon's charge has not won or placed in recent handicap hurdles and 68 days off adds uncertainty around fitness.

runners_data.name: Chasing Crowns
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type by nature, though Harry Sexton's claim makes this interesting — the horse is mapped to midfield through redistribution rather than choice, and its fade-in-finish flag combined with a STYLE_FIT discount makes this one to treat cautiously unless it gets an unusually clean run; form in Good-ground handicaps has been limited.

runners_data.name: Trixaboutmaisie
runners_data.note: Colin Bowe's five-year-old returned just nine days ago and has shown nothing better than seventh across four recent outings, all on Good — a true hold-up runner by inclination that the race shape is likely to push closer to the pace than it prefers, with a STYLE_FIT discount applying.

runners_data.name: Urbs Intacta Manet
runners_data.note: Has a pronounced fading tendency and a poor record on Good ground (2 from 6 sim-going runs in any kind of contention), and 71 days since last seen add significant fitness doubt; J P Flavin's five-year-old carries a STYLE_FIT flag having been nudged towards midfield from its natural rear position.

runners_data.name: Ballinaboola Gold
runners_data.note: Showed a career-best 2nd over 24f on Good ground last time and goes fresh well enough (21 days); Richard Donohoe's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up type repositioned towards midfield by the race shape, and while the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations, it retains each-way claims if it gets a clear passage.

runners_data.name: Talas Kera
runners_data.note: Eoghan Finegan's booking on this John Carr-trained five-year-old is the main angle — the horse has placed twice on Good and handles this trip, but is a hold-up runner shifted closer than ideal; results have been mid-divisional at best and it needs everything to go right.

runners_data.name: Clever Court
runners_data.note: Won last time on Good ground over 20f for P J Rothwell and Shane O'Callaghan claims, and the trend of progression from his recent placed efforts is genuine; races prominently, which is a natural fit for the race shape created by Georgia Celena's solo front-running, and cheekpieces have clearly sparked improvement.

runners_data.name: Phildante
runners_data.note: Joshua Halford takes this nine-year-old for Eoin Doyle — has placed on Good ground over similar trips and tongue-strap plus cheekpieces are in use; a prominent runner who will likely find Georgia Celena's pace hard to pressure, but his consistency score on Good is limited and age may count against him at the end of 3m.

runners_data.name: Cruisin Susan
runners_data.note: Mr J P Berry's amateur booking on this nine-year-old comes after 55 days off, and both the layoff and the fade-in-finish flag are concerns over 3m; a natural hold-up horse displaced to midfield by the redistribution, its best going form is mixed and winning prospects are slim.

runners_data.name: Glaoinn An Airgead
runners_data.note: Reserve rider still attached and only seven days since last run — James Barcoe's eight-year-old has a poor sim-going record (0W 0P from 14 relevant runs) and is another natural hold-up type pushed out of position by the sheer volume of closers in this field; there is little in the form to inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Georgia Celena is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner 3m handicap hurdle and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the off — likely setting a measured tempo over Good ground at Wexford. Fire Coral and Clever Court will press from prominent positions, giving the race some early shape without threatening Georgia Celena's command, while Phildante is also likely to travel in the first half-dozen. The field holds substantially more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Trixaboutmaisie, Chasing Crowns, Urbs Intacta Manet, Ballinaboola Gold, Talas Kera, Glaoinn An Airgead and Cruisin Susan are all natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield because they simply cannot all settle at the back in a 15-runner field, and several will be forced wider and closer than they want to be. With one uncontested leader setting a controlled, honest pace over a stiff 3m trip, this race shape most favours prominent and front-running profiles who travel economically in the first half of the race, conserve energy through the middle, and have enough class to sustain their run from three out — genuine hold-up horses who do get back will face a searching closing test with limited time to reel the leaders in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Georgia Celena dictates a measured tempo and is reeled in only approaching the last, with a prominent racer ready to strike.
scenarios.body: Georgia Celena's uncontested front-running sets up a race where prominent types like Fire Coral and Clever Court travel sweetly in second and third, putting them perfectly placed to challenge from two out; at 3m on Good ground this suits horses who race economically close to the pace rather than having to make up ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Georgia Celena's gallop is truly sustainable and the hold-up brigade is unable to close the deficit from three out.
scenarios.body: With most of the field racing out of their preferred hold-up position and the pace never truly searching, Georgia Celena's jumping and fitness could see her last home ahead of a beaten field; her recent prominent-style form on Good going, combined with the absence of any rival willing to take her on early, gives this genuine viability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Strongly
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop proves fast enough to bring the race to the hold-up brigade and at least one true closer gets a dream run through.
scenarios.body: A handful of natural hold-up types — Desert Cave, Moonlight Paradise and Nashville Notions — are best placed among the rear-guard to produce a late surge if the pace does hot up; however, the redistribution of so many closers to midfield muddies the water, and only those with genuine finishing speed and a clean passage will benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Unravels, Rank Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart through falls, errors or a chaotic pace that dramatically thins the field before the home straight.
scenarios.body: In a 15-runner handicap hurdle with several inconsistent horses and jumping risks, a scrambled race can elevate bottom-weight types who jump cleanly and stay on honestly; Ballinaboola Gold and Talas Kera, both durable sorts at this trip, could find themselves in an unlikely position if attrition takes its toll ahead of them.

watchPoints.text: Georgia Celena jumping — if she makes an error at any of the three flights in the home straight having led throughout, a tight finish could become a scramble among Fire Coral and Clever Court with nothing to aim at.

Trixaboutmaisie, Chasing Crowns and Urbs Intacta Manet are all hold-up horses likely to race closer than they want; watch for traffic jams in the back straight as they bunch in midfield and potentially impede each other or the prominent runners.

Fire Coral's trainer S Curling has a sharp-looking runner here with a strong Good-ground record — if he travels prominently throughout and jumps fluently, he could land a telling blow from two out before the field can regroup.

Clever Court won last time and is the most progressive horse in the field at present — Patrick Rothwell's five-year-old with the claiming rider is worth tracking from the outset to see if he can hold a prominent position and use that winning momentum.

Desert Cave (13 days since last run, 3m trip on Good) is one of the few genuine hold-up types with a realistic chance if the gallop proves genuinely honest — watch where Rian Lane positions him early as a guide to how the pace is being read from the saddle.

races.name: Park Run At Wexford Saturday Mornings Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Duke Otto
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Patrick J Flynn, 154 days off the track which is a concern; holds solid Good-ground form (10/15 sim-going) but needs the pace to collapse in front to land a blow from 8th-plus.|

runners_data.name: Rightfolksplease
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner, absent 537 days and returning with headgear (tongue-tie); has a strong Good-ground profile (12/15) but the massive layoff is the dominant query — if fit enough, the uncontested lead is a genuine asset.|

runners_data.name: Boola Times
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare for David Budds with a fade-in-finish flag; only 7/13 on similar going and her best form has come at longer trips — the 2m½f on Good ground here may not bring out her best.|

runners_data.name: Hatfield Hammer
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan-trained prominent racer back quickly (20 days) and boasting the strongest similar-going record in the field (14/15); ran 3rd over 17f on Good last time and is the archetype for what this pace shape rewards.|

runners_data.name: Bella Union
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old but in career form — won twice on Good ground at this sort of trip and ran 2nd just 20 days ago; John McConnell has him spot-on, he travels prominent and his 14/15 similar-going stat is outstanding.|

runners_data.name: Ranting And Raven
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Gavin Cromwell, only four-year-old in the race; holds a placed record on Good ground but has not won in 15 runs — needs things to go wrong for others in front of him.|

runners_data.name: Davitts Quay
runners_data.note: Anthony Mullins-trained five-year-old with a fade-in-finish concern and a modest 3/4 similar-going sample; has finished no better than 7th in all four Good-ground starts — hard to build a case.|

runners_data.name: Cinnabar Moth
runners_data.note: Liz Doyle five-year-old with a strong 7/8 similar-going stat, but a true hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping because the rear is overcrowded; the style-fit discount (0.90) applies and Richard Deegan will need to improvise to get him competitive.|

runners_data.name: Backinabit
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's seven-year-old won last time out over 17f on Good — the form is there — but carries a fade-in-finish flag and has been redistributed from his natural hold-up berth; the style compromise (0.92) and limited prominent experience temper confidence.|

runners_data.name: Mount Hotham
runners_data.note: Consistently finishing in the 9th-to-14th range on Good ground (5/8 sim-going), a fade flag, and placed into midfield away from his natural position; John Joseph Hanlon runner with very little to recommend him on current evidence.|

runners_data.name: Sidiriya
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride on this PJ Rothwell prominent type who has placed twice in 15 similar-going runs; ran 2nd over 16f on Good two starts ago and 3rd recently — clean jumping and a forward position suit.|

runners_data.name: I'm For Home
runners_data.note: R P Rath's eight-year-old is a true hold-up performer mapped to midfield due to field congestion; Kevin Healy (7) rides and the horse has not won in 15 similar-going starts — the style displacement makes this a very tough ask.|

runners_data.name: Esticky End
runners_data.note: Tom McGuinness's prominent runner finished 2nd over 17f on Good last time out; 10/15 similar-going runs suggests course-type familiarity and Dylan Robinson knows how to place one handily — a quietly interesting place contender.|

races.paceDynamic: Rightfolksplease is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with 537 days off the track, will likely bowl along at a comfortable, uncontested tempo rather than setting a scorching gallop — creating a controlled, single-file procession rather than a true war of attrition. Hatfield Hammer, Bella Union, Sidiriya and Esticky End will press for prominent positions just behind, meaning the early order from second through fifth place will be competitive and could briefly sharpen the pace through the first half-mile. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than can all settle where they want — Cinnabar Moth, Backinabit, Mount Hotham and I'm For Home are genuine hold-up horses forced to map to midfield, meaning the rear of the field will be less congested than it appears and those horses will not be in their ideal position. A sustainable, front-runner-controlled tempo on Good ground over 2m½f at Wexford strongly favours prominent-racing types who can travel handy, avoid traffic, and produce a clean jump at the last — closers relying on a true stamina test are disadvantaged when the pace is this moderate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rightfolksplease Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Rightfolksplease bowls along unchallenged and the prominent trackers cannot close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Rightfolksplease sets an uncontested rhythm on the heels of which Hatfield Hammer and Bella Union travel smoothly; with no rival willing to take it on, the gallop stays honest but not punishing and the horse who jumps cleanly throughout and travels widest into the straight lands it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Posse Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Hatfield Hammer, Bella Union or Sidiriya press Rightfolksplease hard enough from the second flight to briefly sharpen the tempo, then overhaul the leader from two out.
scenarios.body: A slightly more competitive early pace takes the edge off Rightfolksplease's stamina reserves, allowing the prominent chasers tracking in second and third to sweep past jumping the last; horses with strong Good-ground form at this trip and clean jumping records come to the fore.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Lucky
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unexpectedly brisk and the prominent group tie each other up, leaving daylight for a hold-up type to weave through.
scenarios.body: Duke Otto or Ranting And Raven, both genuine hold-up horses not displaced by redistribution, could pick up the pieces if the prominent runners burn out; however, this scenario relies on a stronger pace than one lone front-runner is likely to generate, limiting its probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Cinnabar Moth, Backinabit or I'm For Home — all true hold-up horses forced out of role — somehow navigate wide and produce a late run.
scenarios.body: These horses are racing out of their natural style and carry style-fit discounts of 0.90–0.92, meaning they would need a near-perfect trip and a late collapse by the leaders to get involved; the scenario is possible but structurally unlikely given the moderate tempo and their compromised positioning.

watchPoints.text: Bella Union and Hatfield Hammer are both prominent-profile horses with the best similar-going records in the race (14/15 each) — if either jumps fluently from the front rank, they are the biggest dangers to each other and to everything else.|

Rightfolksplease's 537-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race — if fitness is lacking, the horse could stop quickly after the second last and leave the race wide open for the prominent chasers.|

Backinabit won last time out and carries live form, but the fade-in-finish flag combined with being displaced from a natural hold-up role means punters should check whether Daniel King attempts to ride him more prominently than usual.|

Duke Otto was pulled up last time and has not run in 154 days — Peter Smithers (7) should be watched in the early stages to see if the horse travels or is immediately struggling, which would confirm or remove him as a live factor.|

The Going Report confirms consistent Good ground across all races on the card — no late-softening risk, meaning prominent types who travel on a sound surface retain their structural advantage throughout the afternoon.|

races.name: Park Run At Wexford Saturday Mornings Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Del Boys Diva
runners_data.note: Shane Crawley in fair recent form (1/2 over 14 days) and this 6yo returns after just 17 days; a natural hold-up horse with a stamina concern flagged at the finish, but sim-going record of 1W1P on Good suggests the surface suits — best chance if she travels smoothly off the pace and delivers one clean run.|

runners_data.name: Tropical Twist
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott and that stable angle is always worth noting in Irish handicap hurdles; genuine hold-up type whose sim-going record is 0W0P on Good over this trip, and the form string of 45FP-5 is uninspiring — requires everything to fall right from the rear.|

runners_data.name: Glendower
runners_data.note: Paddy Cody (7lb claimer) reduces the burden for Eoin Doyle's 5yo, who has shown flashes of ability over shorter (3rd on Good at 10f) but the step back up to 2m½f is untested in recent runs; races hold-up but has placed four times in last five runs, suggesting consistency if not outright class.|

runners_data.name: Let It Settle
runners_data.note: Harry Sexton (7lb claimer) partners Thomas Hughes' 5yo on a quick turnaround of 13 days; flagged as a fade-in-finish type which is damaging in a race likely to be run at a steady pace that suddenly quickens — sim-going of 0W1P on Good and a recent 2nd the sole encouragement, but the finishing style is a major concern.|

runners_data.name: Victoria Kesia
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's 5yo is a genuine hold-up horse placed into midfield by the race shape — her natural position at the rear is compromised by the field's cluster of closers; best effort was 3rd over 18f on Good, suggesting the trip could be her ally if she finds daylight in time.|

runners_data.name: Polly Poppins
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race, and that tactical position is worth its weight in gold in a 12-runner field of closers; raced 1 day ago which is a notable freshness flag, and her sim-going record of 14/15 on Good is extensive exposure — she knows this track and trip well enough to set a measured gallop.|

runners_data.name: Eastern Blue Bird
runners_data.note: Richard Condon (5lb claimer) partners P A Fahy's 5yo, who is a true hold-up type placed into midfield by necessity rather than design; sim-going record entirely on Good (though course was STA in recent runs) and a modest hurdle form figure of 6/047 makes it hard to make a case without a significant improvement in jumping.|

runners_data.name: Syosset
runners_data.note: Flagged as a fade-in-finish type and wearing headgear (h), which is a concern for a hold-up horse pushed forward against its nature; Alex Harvey rides for John C McConnell, and a 3rd last time on Good is the best recent effort — the STA-ground placings may flatter given this is a Good surface today.|

runners_data.name: Light Her Up
runners_data.note: Hugh Paul Finegan's 8yo returns after just 2 days, which is an unusually quick turnaround and a stamina/freshness flag worth respecting; fitted with tongue-strap and blinkers (tb), runs hold-up but is repositioned to midfield in this shape — sim-going shows 0W1P on Good over longer trips where stamina was tested.|

runners_data.name: Liss Eile
runners_data.note: A fade-in-finish flag and a visor (v) for this Ahern-trained 6yo who has placed just once in 15 sim-going runs on Good — consistency is a significant concern; genuine hold-up horse mapped forward by the race dynamic, and her recent string of 10ths suggests she needs things to fall perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Tasmanian Girl
runners_data.note: Declan Queally's 6yo returns after 57 days, the longest break in the field, fitted with a tongue-strap (t); best win came over 16f on Good for this trainer (1W2P sim-going) but the absence and the tongue-strap addition need explaining — hold-up style pushed into midfield in this shape.|

runners_data.name: Avandra
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell in decent recent form (1/2 over 14 days) and Shane O'Callaghan claims 3lb; a genuine hold-up horse with a blinkered headgear (b) and a 2nd last time on Good over 16f is the standout form figure — low weight and a capable claim give her an each-way profile if she can find daylight from the rear.|

races.paceDynamic: Polly Poppins is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner handicap hurdle over 2m½f at Wexford on Good ground, and with no rival pressing from the front, she is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from flag to finish. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up types, meaning the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to stretch the field early, creating a compressed, processional shape that plays into the hands of horses who can track the leader efficiently rather than those who must make up significant ground late. This race shape clearly favours prominent racers and those who can sit just off the front, as a steady tempo on Good ground over this trip will see the race genuinely begin from the third-last hurdle with stamina and jumping accuracy at a premium. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Victoria Kesia, Syosset, Eastern Blue Bird, Liss Eile, Tasmanian Girl, Light Her Up, and Avandra are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, and in a slow-run race several will find themselves further forward than ideal yet still unable to dominate; Polly Poppins and the handful who track her most closely are best positioned tactically.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Polly Poppins Lone Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Polly Poppins bowls along unchallenged at a steady clip and the race is won by those racing prominently throughout.
scenarios.body: Polly Poppins sets her own fractions on Good ground and her rivals are unable to mount a sustained challenge from deep, leaving horses who tracked her through the race best placed at the last hurdle; the steady tempo and flat Wexford circuit suits those with natural jumping rhythm over this 2m½f trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Launched Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final half-mile and horses coming from mid-division overhaul the tiring leader.
scenarios.body: A sustainable gallop can occasionally become a false crawl that suddenly quickens, leaving those in touch from midfield able to swoop in the final two hurdles; runners like Del Boys Diva and Tropical Twist who travel well off a strong hold-up position could benefit if the race suddenly quickens from the third-last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so modest that Polly Poppins simply idles to victory having never been threatened.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to press Polly Poppins, she conserves energy throughout and her rivals, many of whom are genuine closers racing out of role in a slow-run race, never generate the momentum to reel her in from the back straight; the Good ground and flat track amplify the front-runner's advantage in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the large cluster of hold-up types jostle for position in midfield and disrupted rivals produce an unexpected winner from deep.
scenarios.body: With seven runners effectively racing against their natural style, gaps close, jumping errors multiply, and a horse carrying low weight like Avandra or Light Her Up could scramble into contention amid the disorder; this scenario is the least likely precisely because few of these runners have the profile or form to win by making ground late on a flat Good-ground track.

watchPoints.text: Polly Poppins ran just 1 day ago — watch for signs of fatigue or over-keenness in the early stages that could compromise her ability to control the pace she sets.

The field contains seven genuine hold-up horses competing for a small number of berths in midfield — watch for scrimmaging and bumping on the first circuit as rivals jostle against their natural style.
Syosset wears headgear and is flagged as a fade-in-finish type, yet is mapped to midfield in a slowly-run race — watch for this horse to be prominent early and stop quickly from the third-last.

Avandra carries the lowest weight in the field (145lbs) with a 3lb claimer aboard and showed a recent 2nd on Good over the sim-going — watch to see whether she can find a clear run from the rear before the second-last.
Light Her Up runs just 2 days after her last outing, an unusually tight turnaround for an 8yo — watch for any signs of fatigue or stiffness that could cause jumping errors at a crucial stage.

races.name: Save The Date Ladies Day At Wexford Races Friday 7th August Flat Race
